title: Matthew 1:1
text: A genealogy of Jesus Christ, a descendant of David and Abraham.

title: Matthew 1:2
text: Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac of Jacob, Jacob of Judah and his brothers,

title: Matthew 1:3
text: Judah of Perez and Zerah, whose mother was Tamar, Perez of Hezron, Hezron of Ram,

title: Matthew 1:4
text: Ram of Amminadab, Amminadab of Nashon, Nashon of Salmon,

title: Matthew 1:5
text: Salmon of Boaz, whose mother was Rahab, Boaz of Obed, whose mother was Ruth, Obed of Jesse,

title: Matthew 1:6
text: Jesse of David the King. David was the father of Solomon, whose mother was Uriah's widow,

title: Matthew 1:7
text: Solomon of Rehoboam, Rehoboam of Abijah, Abijah of Asa,

title: Matthew 1:8
text: Asa of Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat of Jehoram, Jehoram of Uzziah,

title: Matthew 1:9
text: Uzziah of Jotham, Jotham of Ahaz, Ahaz of Hezekiah,

title: Matthew 1:10
text: Hezekiah of Manasseh, Manasseh of Ammon, Ammon of Josiah,

title: Matthew 1:11
text: Josiah of Jeconiah and his brothers, at the time of the Exile to Babylon.

title: Matthew 1:12
text: After the Exile to Babylon--Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel, Shealtiel of Zerubbabel,

title: Matthew 1:13
text: Zerubbabel of Abiud, Abiud of Eliakim, Eliakim of Azor,

title: Matthew 1:14
text: Azor of Zadok, Zadok of Achim, Achim of Eliud,

title: Matthew 1:15
text: Eliud of Eleazar, Eleazar of Matthan, Matthan of Jacob,

title: Matthew 1:16
text: Jacob of Joseph, the husband of Mary, who was the mother of Jesus, who is called 'Christ'.

title: Matthew 1:17
text: So the whole number of generations from Abraham to David is fourteen; from David to the Exile to Babylon fourteen; and from the Exile to Babylon to the Christ fourteen.

title: Matthew 1:18
text: The birth of Jesus Christ took place as follows:--His mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, but, before the marriage took place, she found herself to be with child by the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Matthew 1:19
text: Her husband, Joseph, was a religious man and, being unwilling to expose her to contempt, resolved to put an end to their betrothal privately.

title: Matthew 1:20
text: He had been dwelling upon this, when an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. "Joseph, son of David," the angel said, "do not be afraid to take Mary for your wife, for her child has been conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Matthew 1:21
text: She shall give birth to a son; and you shall give him the name Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins."

title: Matthew 1:22
text: All this happened in fulfillment of these words of the Lord in the Prophet, where he says--

title: Matthew 1:23
text: 'Behold! the virgin shall be with child and shall give birth to a son, And they will give him the name Immanuel'--a word which means 'God is with us.'

title: Matthew 1:24
text: When Joseph awoke from his sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord had directed him.

title: Matthew 1:25
text: He made Mary his wife, but did not live with her as her husband until after the birth of her son; and to this son he gave the name Jesus.

title: Matthew 2:1
text: After the birth of Jesus at Bethlehem in Judea, in the reign of King Herod, some Astrologers from the East arrived in Jerusalem, asking:

title: Matthew 2:2
text: "Where is the new-born King of the Jews? for we saw his star in the east, and have come to do homage to him."

title: Matthew 2:3
text: When King Herod heard of this, he was much troubled, and so, too, was all Jerusalem.

title: Matthew 2:4
text: He called together all the Chief Priests and Teachers of the Law in the nation, and questioned them as to where the Christ was to be born.

title: Matthew 2:5
text: "At Bethlehem in Judea," was their answer; "for it is said in the Prophet--

title: Matthew 2:6
text: 'And thou, Bethlehem in Judah's land, Art in no way least among the chief cities of Judah; For out of thee will come a Chieftain- - One who will shepherd my people Israel.'"

title: Matthew 2:7
text: Then Herod secretly sent for the Astrologers, and ascertained from them the date of the appearance of the star;

title: Matthew 2:8
text: And, sending them to Bethlehem, he said: "Go and make careful inquiries about the child, and, as soon as you have found him, bring me word, that I, too, may go and do homage to him."

title: Matthew 2:9
text: The Astrologers heard what the King had to say, and then continued their journey. And the star which they had seen in the east led them on, until it reached, and stood over, the place where the child was.

title: Matthew 2:10
text: At the sight of the star they were filled with joy.

title: Matthew 2:11
text: Entering the house, they saw the child with his mother, Mary, and fell at his feet and did homage to him. Then they unpacked their treasures, and offered to the child presents of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

title: Matthew 2:12
text: But afterwards, having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their own country by another road.

title: Matthew 2:13
text: After they had left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, and said: "Awake, take the child and his mother, and seek refuge in Egypt; and stay there until I bid you return, for Herod is about to search for the child, to put him to death."

title: Matthew 2:14
text: Joseph awoke, and taking the child and his mother by night, went into Egypt,

title: Matthew 2:15
text: And there he stayed until Herod's death; in fulfillment of these words of the Lord in the Prophet, where he says--'Out of Egypt I called my Son.'

title: Matthew 2:16
text: When Herod found that he had been trifled with by the Astrologers, he was very angry. He sent and put to death all the boys in Bethlehem and the whole of that neighborhood, who were two years old or under, guided by the date which he had ascertained from the Astrologers.

title: Matthew 2:17
text: Then were fulfilled these words spoken in the Prophet Jeremiah, where he says--

title: Matthew 2:18
text: 'A voice was heard in Ramah, Weeping and much lamentation; Rachel, weeping for her children, Refused all comfort because they were not.'

title: Matthew 2:19
text: But, on the death of Herod, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, and said:

title: Matthew 2:20
text: "Awake, take the child and his mother, and go into the Land of Israel, for those who sought to take the child's life are dead."

title: Matthew 2:21
text: And he awoke, and taking the child and his mother, went into the Land of Israel.

title: Matthew 2:22
text: But, hearing that Archelaus had succeeded his father Herod as King of Judea, he was afraid to go back there; and having been warned in a dream, he went into the part of the country called Galilee.

title: Matthew 2:23
text: And there he settled in the town of Nazareth, in fulfillment of these words in the Prophets--'He will be called a Nazarene.'

title: Matthew 3:1
text: About that time John the Baptist first appeared, proclaiming in the Wilderness of Judea:

title: Matthew 3:2
text: "Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand."

title: Matthew 3:3
text: This is he who was spoken of in the Prophet Isaiah, where he says--'The voice of one crying aloud in the Wilderness: "Make ready the way of the Lord, Make his paths straight."'

title: Matthew 3:4
text: John wore clothing made of camels' hair, with a belt of leather round his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.

title: Matthew 3:5
text: At that time Jerusalem, and all Judea, as well as the whole district of the Jordan, went out to him

title: Matthew 3:6
text: And were baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.

title: Matthew 3:7
text: When, however, John saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to receive his baptism, he said to them: "You brood of vipers! Who has prompted you to seek refuge from the coming judgement?

title: Matthew 3:8
text: Let your life, then, prove your repentance;

title: Matthew 3:9
text: And do not think that you can say among yourselves 'Abraham is our ancestor,' for I tell you that out of these very stones God is able to raise descendants for Abraham!

title: Matthew 3:10
text: Already the axe is lying at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that fails to bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.

title: Matthew 3:11
text: I, indeed, baptize you with water to teach repentance; but He who is Coming after me is more powerful than I, and I am not fit even to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

title: Matthew 3:12
text: His winnowing-fan is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing-floor, and store his grain in the barn, but the chaff he will burn with inextinguishable fire."

title: Matthew 3:13
text: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.

title: Matthew 3:14
text: But John tried to prevent him. "It is I," he said, "who need to be baptized by you; why then do you come to me?"

title: Matthew 3:15
text: "Let it be so for the present," Jesus answered, "since it is fitting for us thus to satisfy every claim of religion." Upon this, John consented.

title: Matthew 3:16
text: After the baptism of Jesus, and just as he came up from the water, the heavens opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending, like a dove, and alighting upon him,

title: Matthew 3:17
text: And from the heavens there came a voice which said: "This is my son, the Beloved, in whom I delight."

title: Matthew 4:1
text: Then Jesus was led up into the Wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the Devil.

title: Matthew 4:2
text: And, after he had fasted for forty days and forty nights, he became hungry.

title: Matthew 4:3
text: And the Tempter came to him, and said: "If you are God's Son, tell these stones to become loaves of bread."

title: Matthew 4:4
text: But Jesus answered: "Scripture says--'It is not on bread alone that man is to live, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.' "

title: Matthew 4:5
text: Then the Devil took him to the Holy City, and, placing him on the parapet of the temple, said to him:

title: Matthew 4:6
text: "If you are God's Son, throw yourself down, for Scripture says- -'He will give his angels commands about thee, And on their hands they will upbear thee, Lest ever thou shouldst strike thy foot against a stone.' "

title: Matthew 4:7
text: "Scripture also says," answered Jesus, "Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.'"

title: Matthew 4:8
text: The third time, the Devil took Jesus to a very high mountain, and, showing him all the kingdoms of the world and their splendor, said to him:

title: Matthew 4:9
text: "All these I will give you, if you will fall at my feet and do homage to me."

title: Matthew 4:10
text: Then Jesus said to him: "Begone, Satan! for Scripture says-- 'Thou shalt do homage to the Lord thy God, and worship him only.'"

title: Matthew 4:11
text: Then the Devil left him alone, and angels came and ministered to him.

title: Matthew 4:12
text: When Jesus heard that John had been committed to prison, he retired to Galilee.

title: Matthew 4:13
text: Afterwards, leaving Nazareth, he went and settled at Capernaum, which is by the side of the Sea, within the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali;

title: Matthew 4:14
text: In fulfillment of these words in the Prophet Isaiah--

title: Matthew 4:15
text: 'The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, The land of the Road by the Sea, and beyond the Jordan, With Galilee of the Gentiles--

title: Matthew 4:16
text: The people who were dwelling in darkness Have seen a great Light, And, for those who were dwelling in the shadow-land of Death, A Light has risen!'

title: Matthew 4:17
text: At that time Jesus began to proclaim-- "Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand."

title: Matthew 4:18
text: As Jesus was walking along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers--Simon, also known as Peter, and his brother Andrew--casting a net into the Sea; for they were fishermen.

title: Matthew 4:19
text: "Come and follow me," Jesus said, " and I will set you to fish for men."

title: Matthew 4:20
text: The two men left their nets at once and followed him.

title: Matthew 4:21
text: Going further on, he saw two other men who were also brothers, James, Zebediah's son, and his brother John, in their boat with their father, mending their nets. Jesus called them,

title: Matthew 4:22
text: And they at once left their boat and their father, and followed him.

title: Matthew 4:23
text: And Jesus went all through Galilee, teaching in their Synagogues, proclaiming the Good News of the Kingdom, and curing every kind of disease and every kind of sickness among the people;

title: Matthew 4:24
text: And his fame spread all through Syria. They brought to him all who were ill with any form of disease, or who were suffering pain--any who were either possessed by demons, or were lunatic, or paralyzed; and he cured them.

title: Matthew 4:25
text: And he was followed by large crowds from Galilee, the district of the Ten Towns, Jerusalem, Judea, and from beyond the Jordan.

title: Matthew 5:1
text: On seeing the crowds of People, Jesus went up the hill; and, when he had taken his seat, his disciples came up to him;

title: Matthew 5:2
text: And he began to teach them as follows:

title: Matthew 5:3
text: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

title: Matthew 5:4
text: Blessed are the mourners, for they shall be comforted.

title: Matthew 5:5
text: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.

title: Matthew 5:6
text: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied.

title: Matthew 5:7
text: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall find mercy.

title: Matthew 5:8
text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

title: Matthew 5:9
text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called Sons of God.

title: Matthew 5:10
text: Blessed are those who have been persecuted in the cause of righteousness, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

title: Matthew 5:11
text: Blessed are you when people taunt you, and persecute you, and say everything evil about you--untruly, and on my account.

title: Matthew 5:12
text: Be glad and rejoice, because your reward in Heaven will be great; for so men persecuted the Prophets who lived before you.

title: Matthew 5:13
text: It is you who are the Salt of the earth; but, if the salt should lose its strength, what will you use to restore its saltiness? It is no longer good for anything, but is thrown away, and trampled underfoot.

title: Matthew 5:14
text: It is you who are the Light of the world. A town that stands on a hill cannot be hidden.

title: Matthew 5:15
text: Men do not light a lamp and put it under the corn-measure, but on the lamp-stand, where it gives light to every one in the house.

title: Matthew 5:16
text: Let your light so shine before the eyes of your fellow men, that, seeing your good actions, they may praise your Father who is in Heaven.

title: Matthew 5:17
text: Do not think that I have come to do away with the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to do away with them, but to complete them.

title: Matthew 5:18
text: For I tell you, until the heavens and the earth disappear, not even the smallest letter, nor one stroke of a letter, shall disappear from the Law until all is done.

title: Matthew 5:19
text: Whoever, therefore, breaks one of these commandments, even the least of them, and teaches others to do so, will be the least- esteemed in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever keeps them, and teaches others to do so, will be esteemed great in the Kingdom of Heaven.

title: Matthew 5:20
text: Indeed I tell you that, unless your religion is above that of the Teachers of the Law, and Pharisees, you will never enter the Kingdom of Heaven.

title: Matthew 5:21
text: You have heard that to our ancestors it was said--'Thou shalt not commit murder,' and 'Whoever commits murder shall be liable to answer for it to the Court.'

title: Matthew 5:22
text: I, however, say to you that any one who cherishes anger against his brother shall be liable to answer for it to the Court; and whoever pours contempt upon his brother shall be liable to answer for it to the High Council, while whoever calls down curses upon him shall be liable to answer for it in the fiery Pit.

title: Matthew 5:23
text: Therefore, when presenting your gift at the altar, if even there you remember that your brother has some grievance against you,

title: Matthew 5:24
text: Leave your gift there, before the altar, go and be reconciled to your brother, first, then come and present your gift.

title: Matthew 5:25
text: Be ready to make friends with your opponent, even when you meet him on your way to the court; for fear that he should hand you over to the judge, and the judge to his officer, and you should be thrown into prison.

title: Matthew 5:26
text: I tell you, you will not come out until you have paid the last penny.

title: Matthew 5:27
text: You have heard that it was said--'Thou shalt not commit adultery.'

title: Matthew 5:28
text: I, however, say to you that any one who looks at a woman with an impure intention has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

title: Matthew 5:29
text: If your right eye is a snare to you, take it out and throw it away. It would be best for you to lose one part of your body, and not to have the whole of it thrown into the Pit.

title: Matthew 5:30
text: And, if your right hand is a snare to you, cut it off and throw it away. It would be best for you to lose one part of your body, and not to have the whole of it go down to the Pit.

title: Matthew 5:31
text: It was also said--'Let any one who divorces his wife serve her with a notice of separation.'

title: Matthew 5:32
text: I, however, say to you that any one who divorces his wife, except on the ground of her unchastity, leads to her committing adultery; while any one who marries her after her divorce is guilty of adultery.

title: Matthew 5:33
text: Again, you have heard that to our ancestors it was said--'Thou shalt not break an oath, but thou shall keep thine oaths as a debt due to the Lord.'

title: Matthew 5:34
text: I, however, say to you that you must not swear at all, either by Heaven, since that is God's throne,

title: Matthew 5:35
text: Or by the earth, since that is his footstool, or by Jerusalem, since that is the city of the Great King.

title: Matthew 5:36
text: Nor should you swear by your head, since you cannot make a single hair either white or black.

title: Matthew 5:37
text: Let your words be simply 'Yes' or 'No'; anything beyond this comes from what is wrong.

title: Matthew 5:38
text: You have heard that it was said--'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.'

title: Matthew 5:39
text: I, however, say to you that you must not resist wrong; but, if any one strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to him also;

title: Matthew 5:40
text: And, when any one wants to go to law with you, to take your coat, let him have your cloak as well;

title: Matthew 5:41
text: And, if any one compels you to go one mile, go two miles with him.

title: Matthew 5:42
text: Give to him who asks of you; and, from him who wants to borrow from you, do not turn away.

title: Matthew 5:43
text: You have heard that it was said--'Thou shalt love thy neighbor and hate thy enemy.'

title: Matthew 5:44
text: I, however, say to you--Love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,

title: Matthew 5:45
text: That you may become Sons of your Father who is in Heaven; for he causes his sun to rise upon bad and good alike, and sends rain upon the righteous and upon the unrighteous.

title: Matthew 5:46
text: For, if you love only those who love you, what reward will you have? Even the tax-gatherers do this!

title: Matthew 5:47
text: And, if you show courtesy to your brothers only, what are you doing more than others? Even the Gentiles do this!

title: Matthew 5:48
text: You, then, must become perfect--as your heavenly Father is perfect.

title: Matthew 6:1
text: Take care not to perform your religious duties in public in order to be seen by others; if you do, your Father who is in Heaven has no reward for you.

title: Matthew 6:2
text: Therefore, when you do acts of charity, do not have a trumpet blown in front of you, as hypocrites do in the Synagogues and in the streets, that they may be praised by others. There, I tell you, is their reward!

title: Matthew 6:3
text: But, when you do acts of charity, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

title: Matthew 6:4
text: So that your charity may be secret; and your Father, who sees what is in secret, will recompense you.

title: Matthew 6:5
text: And, when you pray, you are not to behave as hypocrites do. They like to pray standing in the Synagogues and at the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. There, I tell you, is their reward!

title: Matthew 6:6
text: But, when one of you prays, let him go into his own room, shut the door, and pray to his Father who dwells in secret; and his Father, who sees what is secret, will recompense him.

title: Matthew 6:7
text: When praying, do not repeat the same words over and over again, as is done by the Gentiles, who think that by using many words they will obtain a hearing.

title: Matthew 6:8
text: Do not imitate them; for God, your Father, knows what you need before you ask him.

title: Matthew 6:9
text: You, therefore, should pray thus--'Our Father, who art in Heaven, May thy name be held holy,

title: Matthew 6:10
text: Thy Kingdom come, thy will be done--on earth, as in Heaven.

title: Matthew 6:11
text: Give us to-day the bread that we shall need;

title: Matthew 6:12
text: And forgive us our wrong-doings, as we have forgiven those who have wronged us;

title: Matthew 6:13
text: And take us not into temptation, but deliver us from Evil.'

title: Matthew 6:14
text: For, if you forgive others their offences, your heavenly Father will forgive you also;

title: Matthew 6:15
text: But, if you do not forgive others their offences, not even your Father will forgive your offences.

title: Matthew 6:16
text: And, when you fast, do not put on gloomy looks, as hypocrites do who disfigure their faces that they may be seen by men to be fasting. That, I tell you, is their reward!

title: Matthew 6:17
text: But, when one of your fasts, let him anoint his head and wash his face,

title: Matthew 6:18
text: That he may not be seen by men to be fasting, but by his Father who dwells in secret; and his Father, who sees what is secret, will recompense him.

title: Matthew 6:19
text: Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.

title: Matthew 6:20
text: But store up treasures for yourselves in Heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break in or steal.

title: Matthew 6:21
text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

title: Matthew 6:22
text: The lamp of the body is the eye. If your eye is unclouded, your whole body will be lit up;

title: Matthew 6:23
text: But, if your eye is diseased, your whole body will be darkened. And, if the inner light is darkness, how intense must that darkness be!

title: Matthew 6:24
text: No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate one and love the other, or else he will attach himself to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and Money.

title: Matthew 6:25
text: That is why I say to you, Do not be anxious about your life here--what you can get to eat or drink; nor yet about your body-- what you can get to wear. Is not life more than food, and the body than its clothing?

title: Matthew 6:26
text: Look at the wild birds--they neither sow, nor reap, nor gather into barns; and yet your heavenly Father feeds them! And are not you more precious than they?

title: Matthew 6:27
text: But which of you, by being anxious, can prolong his life a single moment?

title: Matthew 6:28
text: And why be anxious about clothing? Study the wild lilies, and how they grow. They neither toil nor spin;

title: Matthew 6:29
text: Yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his splendor was not robed like one of these.

title: Matthew 6:30
text: If God so clothes even the grass of the field, which is living to-day and to-morrow will be thrown into the oven, will not he much more clothe you, O men of little faith?

title: Matthew 6:31
text: Do not then ask anxiously 'What can we get to eat?' or 'What can we get to drink?' or 'What can we get to wear?'

title: Matthew 6:32
text: All these are the things for which the nations are seeking, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

title: Matthew 6:33
text: But first seek his Kingdom and the righteousness that he requires, and then all these things shall be added for you.

title: Matthew 6:34
text: Therefore do not be anxious about to-morrow, for to-morrow will bring its own anxieties. Every day has trouble enough of its own.

title: Matthew 7:1
text: Do not judge, that you may not be judged.

title: Matthew 7:2
text: For, just as you judge others, you will yourselves be judged, and the measure that you mete will be meted out to you.

title: Matthew 7:3
text: And why do you look at the straw in your brother's eye, while you pay no attention at all to the beam in yours?

title: Matthew 7:4
text: How will you say to your brother 'Let me take out the straw from your eye,' when all the time there is a beam in your own?

title: Matthew 7:5
text: Hypocrite! Take out the beam from your own eye first, and then you will see clearly how to take out the straw from your brother's.

title: Matthew 7:6
text: Do not give what is sacred to dogs; nor yet throw your pearls before pigs, lest they should trample them under their feet, and then turn and attack you.

title: Matthew 7:7
text: Ask, and your prayer shall be granted; search, and you shall find; knock, and the door shall be opened to you.

title: Matthew 7:8
text: For he that asks receives, he that searches finds, and to him that knocks the door shall be opened.

title: Matthew 7:9
text: Who among you, when his son asks him for a loaf, will give him a stone,

title: Matthew 7:10
text: Or when he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?

title: Matthew 7:11
text: If you, then, wicked though you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in Heaven give what is good to those that ask him!

title: Matthew 7:12
text: Do to others whatever you would wish them to do to you; for that is the teaching of both the Law and the Prophets.

title: Matthew 7:13
text: Go in by the small gate. Broad and spacious is the road that leads to destruction, and those that go in by it are many;

title: Matthew 7:14
text: For small is the gate, and narrow the road, that leads to Life, and those that find it are few.

title: Matthew 7:15
text: Beware of false Teachers--men who come to you in the guise of sheep, but at heart they are ravenous wolves.

title: Matthew 7:16
text: By the fruit of their lives you will know them. Do people gather grapes from thorn bushes, or figs from thistles?

title: Matthew 7:17
text: So, too, every sound tree bears good fruit, while a worthless tree bears bad fruit.

title: Matthew 7:18
text: A sound tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a worthless tree bear good fruit.

title: Matthew 7:19
text: Every tree that fails to bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

title: Matthew 7:20
text: Hence it is by the fruit of their lives that you will know such men.

title: Matthew 7:21
text: Not every one who says to me 'Master! Master!' will enter the Kingdom of Heaven, but only he who does the will of my Father who is in Heaven.

title: Matthew 7:22
text: On 'That Day' many will say to me 'Master, Master, was not it in your name that we taught, and in your name that we drove out demons, and in your name that we did many miracles?'

title: Matthew 7:23
text: And then I shall say to them plainly 'I never knew you. Go from my presence, you who live in sin.'

title: Matthew 7:24
text: Everyone, therefore, that listens to this teaching of mine and acts upon it may be compared to a prudent man, who built his house upon the rock.

title: Matthew 7:25
text: The rain poured down, the rivers rose, the winds blew and beat upon that house, but it did not fall, for its foundations were upon the rock.

title: Matthew 7:26
text: And every one that listens to this teaching of mine and does not act upon it may be compared to a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.

title: Matthew 7:27
text: The rain poured down, the rivers rose, the winds blew and struck against that house, and it fell; and great was its downfall."

title: Matthew 7:28
text: By the time that Jesus had finished speaking, the crowd was filled with amazement at his teaching.

title: Matthew 7:29
text: For he taught them like one who had authority, and not like their Teachers of the Law.

title: Matthew 8:1
text: When Jesus had come down from the hill, great crowds followed him.

title: Matthew 8:2
text: And he saw a leper who came up, and bowed to the ground before him, and said: "Master, if only you are willing, you are able to make me clean."

title: Matthew 8:3
text: Stretching out his hand, Jesus touched him, saying as he did so: "I am willing; become clean." Instantly he was made clean from his leprosy;

title: Matthew 8:4
text: And then Jesus said to him: "Be careful not to say a word to any one, but go and show yourself to the Priest, and offer the gift directed by Moses, as evidence of your cure."

title: Matthew 8:5
text: After Jesus had entered Capernaum, a Captain in the Roman army came up to him, entreating his help.

title: Matthew 8:6
text: "Sir," he said, "my manservant is lying ill at my house with a stroke of paralysis, and is suffering terribly."

title: Matthew 8:7
text: "I will come and cure him," answered Jesus.

title: Matthew 8:8
text: "Sir," the Captain went on, "I am unworthy to receive you under my roof; but only speak, and my manservant will be cured.

title: Matthew 8:9
text: For I myself am a man under the orders of others, with soldiers under me; and, if I say to one of them 'Go,' he goes, and to another 'Come,' he comes, and to my slave 'Do this,' he does it."

title: Matthew 8:10
text: Jesus was surprised to hear this, and said to those who were following him: "Never I tell you, in any Israelite have I met with such faith as this!

title: Matthew 8:11
text: Yes, and many will come in from East and West and take their places beside Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in the Kingdom of Heaven;

title: Matthew 8:12
text: While the heirs to the Kingdom will be 'banished into the darkness' outside; there, there will be weeping and grinding of teeth."

title: Matthew 8:13
text: Then Jesus said to the Captain: "Go now, and it shall be according to your faith." And the man was cured that very hour.

title: Matthew 8:14
text: When Jesus went into Peter's house, he saw Peter's mother-in- law prostrated with fever.

title: Matthew 8:15
text: On his taking her hand, the fever left her, and she rose and began to wait upon him.

title: Matthew 8:16
text: In the evening the people brought to Jesus many who were possessed by demons; and he drove out the spirits with a word, And cured all who were ill,

title: Matthew 8:17
text: In fulfillment of these words in the Prophet Isaiah--'He took our infirmities on himself, and bore the burden of our diseases.'

title: Matthew 8:18
text: Seeing a crowd round him, Jesus gave orders to go across.

title: Matthew 8:19
text: And a Teacher of the Law came up to him, and said: "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."

title: Matthew 8:20
text: "Foxes have holes," answered Jesus, "and wild birds their roosting-places, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."

title: Matthew 8:21
text: "Master," said another, who was a disciple, "let me first go and bury my father."

title: Matthew 8:22
text: But Jesus answered: "Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their dead."

title: Matthew 8:23
text: Then he got into the boat, followed by his disciples.

title: Matthew 8:24
text: Suddenly so great a storm came on upon the Sea, that the waves broke right over the boat. But Jesus was asleep;

title: Matthew 8:25
text: And the disciples came and roused him. "Master," they cried, "save us; we are lost!"

title: Matthew 8:26
text: "Why are you so timid?" he said. "O men of little faith!" Then Jesus rose and rebuked the winds and the sea, and a great calm followed.

title: Matthew 8:27
text: The men were amazed, and exclaimed: "What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!"

title: Matthew 8:28
text: And on getting to the other side--the country of the Gadarenes--Jesus met two men who were possessed by demons, coming out of the tombs. They were so violent that no one was able to pass that way.

title: Matthew 8:29
text: Suddenly they shrieked out: "What do you want with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before our time?"

title: Matthew 8:30
text: A long way off, there was a drove of many pigs, feeding;

title: Matthew 8:31
text: And the foul spirits began begging Jesus: "If you drive us out, send us into the drove of pigs."

title: Matthew 8:32
text: "Go," he said. The spirits came out, and entered the pigs; and the whole drove rushed down the steep slope into the Sea, and died in the water.

title: Matthew 8:33
text: At this the men who tended them ran away and went to the town, carrying the news of all that had occurred, and of what had happened to the possessed men.

title: Matthew 8:34
text: At the news the whole town went out to meet Jesus, and, when they saw him, they entreated him to go away from their neighborhood.

title: Matthew 9:1
text: Afterwards Jesus got into a boat, and, crossing over, came to his own city.

title: Matthew 9:2
text: And there some people brought to him a paralyzed man on a bed. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the man: "Courage, Child! Your sins are forgiven."

title: Matthew 9:3
text: Then some of the teachers of the Law said to themselves: "This man is blaspheming!"

title: Matthew 9:4
text: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus exclaimed: "Why do your cherish such wicked thoughts?

title: Matthew 9:5
text: Which, I ask, is the easier?--to say 'Your sins are forgiven'? or to say 'Get up, and walk about'?

title: Matthew 9:6
text: But, that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins"--then he said to the paralyzed man--"Get up, take up your bed, and return to your home."

title: Matthew 9:7
text: The man got up and went to his home.

title: Matthew 9:8
text: When the crowd saw this, they were awe-struck, and praised God for giving such power to men.

title: Matthew 9:9
text: As Jesus went along, he saw a man, called Matthew, sitting in the tax-office, and said to him: "Follow me." Matthew got up and followed him.

title: Matthew 9:10
text: And, later on, when he was at table in the house, a number of tax-gatherers and outcasts came in and took their places at table with Jesus and his disciples.

title: Matthew 9:11
text: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples: "Why does your Teacher eat in the company of tax-gatherers and outcasts?"

title: Matthew 9:12
text: On hearing this, Jesus said: "It is not those who are in health that need a doctor, but those who are ill.

title: Matthew 9:13
text: Go and learn what this means--'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice'; for I did not come to call the religious, but the outcast."

title: Matthew 9:14
text: Then John's disciples came to Jesus, and asked: "Why do we and the Pharisees fast while your disciples do not?"

title: Matthew 9:15
text: Jesus answered: "Can the bridegroom's friends mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come, when the bridegroom will be parted from them, and they will fast then.

title: Matthew 9:16
text: No man ever puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for such a patch tears away from the garment, and a worse rent is made.

title: Matthew 9:17
text: Nor do people put new wine into old wine-skins; for, if they do, the skins burst, and the wine runs out, and the skins are lost; but they put new wine into fresh skins, and so both are preserved."

title: Matthew 9:18
text: While Jesus was saying this, a President of a Synagogue came up and bowed to the ground before him. "My daughter," he said, "Has just died; but come and place your hand on her, and she will be restored to life."

title: Matthew 9:19
text: So Jesus rose and followed him, and his disciples went also.

title: Matthew 9:20
text: But meanwhile a woman, who had been suffering from hemorrhage for twelve years, came up behind and touched the tassel of his cloak.

title: Matthew 9:21
text: "If I only touch his cloak," she said to herself, "I shall get well."

title: Matthew 9:22
text: Turning and seeing her, Jesus said: "Courage, Daughter! your faith has delivered you." And the woman was delivered from her malady from that very hour.

title: Matthew 9:23
text: When Jesus reached the President's house, seeing the flute- players, and a number of people all in confusion,

title: Matthew 9:24
text: He said: "Go away, the little girl is not dead; she is asleep." They began to laugh at him;

title: Matthew 9:25
text: But, when the people had been sent out, Jesus went in, and took the little girl's hand, and she rose.

title: Matthew 9:26
text: The report of this spread through all that part of the country.

title: Matthew 9:27
text: As Jesus was passing on from there, he was followed by two blind men, who kept calling out: "Take pity on us, Son of David!"

title: Matthew 9:28
text: When he had gone indoors, the blind men came up to him; and Jesus asked them: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" "Yes, Master!" they answered.

title: Matthew 9:29
text: Upon that he touched their eyes, and said: "It shall be according to your faith." 9:30 Then their eyes were opened. Jesus sternly cautioned them. "See that no one knows of it," he said.

title: Matthew 9:31
text: But the men went out, and spread the news about him through all that part of the country.

title: Matthew 9:32
text: Just as they were going out, some people brought up to Jesus a dumb man who was possessed by a demon;

title: Matthew 9:33
text: And, as soon as the demon had been driven out, the dumb man spoke. The people were astonished at this, and exclaimed: "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!"

title: Matthew 9:34
text: But the Pharisees said: "He drives out the demons by the help of the chief of the demons."  9:35 Jesus went round all the towns and the villages, teaching in their Synagogues, proclaiming the Good News of the Kingdom, and curing every kind of disease and every kind of sickness.

title: Matthew 9:36
text: But, when he saw the crowds, his heart was moved with compassion for them, because they were distressed and harassed, 'like sheep without a shepherd';

title: Matthew 9:37
text: And he said to his disciples: "The harvest is abundant, but the laborers are few.

title: Matthew 9:38
text: Therefore pray to the Owner of the harvest to send laborers to gather in his harvest."

title: Matthew 10:1
text: Calling his twelve Disciples to him, Jesus gave them authority over foul spirits, so that they could drive them out, as well as the power of curing every kind of disease and every kind of sickness.

title: Matthew 10:2
text: The names of the twelve Apostles are these: First Simon, also known as Peter, and his brother Andrew; James the son of Zebediah, and his brother John;

title: Matthew 10:3
text: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax-gather; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;

title: Matthew 10:4
text: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot--the Apostle who betrayed him.

title: Matthew 10:5
text: These twelve Jesus sent out as his Messengers, after giving them these instructions--"Do not go to the Gentiles, nor enter any Samaritan town,

title: Matthew 10:6
text: But make your way rather to the lost sheep of Israel.

title: Matthew 10:7
text: And on your way proclaim that the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.

title: Matthew 10:8
text: Cure the sick, raise the dead, make the lepers clean, drive out demons. You have received free of cost, give free of cost.

title: Matthew 10:9
text: Do not provide yourselves with gold, or silver, or pence in your purses;

title: Matthew 10:10
text: Not even with a bag for the journey, or a change of clothes, or sandals, or even a staff; for the worker is worth his food.

title: Matthew 10:11
text: Whatever town or village you visit, find out who is worthy in that place, and remain there till you leave.

title: Matthew 10:12
text: As you enter the house, greet it.

title: Matthew 10:13
text: Then, if the house is worthy, let your blessing rest upon it, but, if it is unworthy, let your blessing return upon yourselves.

title: Matthew 10:14
text: If no one welcomes you, or listens to what you say, as you leave that house or that town, shake off its dust from your feet.

title: Matthew 10:15
text: I tell you, the doom of the land of Sodom and Gomorrah will be more bearable in the 'Day of Judgement' than the doom of that town.

title: Matthew 10:16
text: Remember, I am sending you out as my Messengers like sheep among wolves. So be as wise as serpents, and as blameless as doves.

title: Matthew 10:17
text: Be on your guard against your fellow men, for they will betray you to courts of law, and scourge you in their Synagogues;

title: Matthew 10:18
text: And you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, that you may witness for me before them and the nations.

title: Matthew 10:19
text: Whenever they betray you, do not be anxious as to how you shall speak or what you shall say, for what you shall say will be given you at the moment;

title: Matthew 10:20
text: For it will not be you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father that speaks within you.

title: Matthew 10:21
text: Brother will betray brother to death, and the father his child; and children will turn against their parents, and cause them to be put to death;

title: Matthew 10:22
text: And you will be hated by every one on account of my Name. Yet the man that endures to the end shall be saved.

title: Matthew 10:23
text: But, when they persecute you in one town, escape to the next; for, I tell you, you will not have come to the end of the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

title: Matthew 10:24
text: A scholar is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.

title: Matthew 10:25
text: It is enough for a scholar to be treated like his teacher, and a servant like his master. If the head of the house has been called Baal-zebub, how much more the members of his household!

title: Matthew 10:26
text: Do not, therefore, be afraid of them. There is nothing concealed which will not be revealed, nor anything hidden which will not become known.

title: Matthew 10:27
text: What I tell you in the dark, say again in the light; and what is whispered in your ear, proclaim upon the housetops.

title: Matthew 10:28
text: And do not be afraid of those who kill the body, but are unable to kill the soul; rather be afraid of him who is able to destroy both soul and body in the Pit.

title: Matthew 10:29
text: Are not two sparrows sold for a half-penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground without your Father's knowledge.

title: Matthew 10:30
text: While as for you, the very hairs of your head are numbered.

title: Matthew 10:31
text: Do not, therefore, be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.

title: Matthew 10:32
text: Every one, therefore, who shall acknowledge me before his fellow men, I, too, will acknowledge before my Father who is in Heaven;

title: Matthew 10:33
text: But, if any one disowns me before his fellow men, I, too, will disown him before my Father who is in Heaven.

title: Matthew 10:34
text: Do not imagine that I have come to bring peace upon the earth. I have come to bring, not peace, but the sword.

title: Matthew 10:35
text: For I have come to set--'a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

title: Matthew 10:36
text: A man's enemies will be the members of his own household.'

title: Matthew 10:37
text: He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

title: Matthew 10:38
text: And the man who does not take his cross and follow in my steps is not worthy of me.

title: Matthew 10:39
text: He who has found his life will lose it, while he who, for my sake, has lost his life shall find it.

title: Matthew 10:40
text: He who welcomes you is welcoming me; and he who welcomes me is welcoming him who sent me as his Messenger.

title: Matthew 10:41
text: He who welcomes a Prophet, because he is a Prophet, shall receive a Prophet's reward; and he who welcomes a good man, because he is a good man, shall receive a good man's reward.

title: Matthew 10:42
text: And, if any one gives but a cup of cold water to one of these lowly ones because he is a disciple, I tell you that he shall assuredly not lose his reward."

title: Matthew 11:1
text: After Jesus had finished giving directions to his twelve Disciples, he left that place in order to teach and preach in their towns.

title: Matthew 11:2
text: Now John had heard in prison what the Christ was doing, and he sent a message by his disciples,

title: Matthew 11:3
text: And asked--" Are you 'The Coming One,' or are we to look for someone else?"

title: Matthew 11:4
text: The answer of Jesus to the question was--" Go and report to John what you hear and see--

title: Matthew 11:5
text: The blind recover their sight and the lame walk, the lepers are made clean and the deaf hear, the dead, too, are raised to life, and the good news is told to the poor.

title: Matthew 11:6
text: And blessed is the man who finds no hindrance in me."

title: Matthew 11:7
text: While these men were going back, Jesus began to say to the crowds with reference to John:

title: Matthew 11:8
text: "What did you go out into the Wilderness to look at? A reed waving in the wind? If not, what did you go out to see? A man richly dressed? Why, those who wear rich things are to be found in the courts of kings!

title: Matthew 11:9
text: What, then, did you go for? To see a Prophet? Yes, I tell you, and far more than a Prophet.

title: Matthew 11:10
text: This is the man of whom Scripture says--'Behold, I am myself sending my Messenger before thy face, And he shall prepare thy way before thee.'

title: Matthew 11:11
text: I tell you, no one born of a woman has yet appeared who is greater than John the Baptist; and yet the lowliest in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.

title: Matthew 11:12
text: From the time of John the Baptist to this very hour, the Kingdom of Heaven has been taken by force, and men using force have been seizing it.

title: Matthew 11:13
text: For the teaching of all the Prophets and of the Law continued till the time of John;

title: Matthew 11:14
text: And--if you are ready to accept it--John is himself the Elijah who was destined to come.

title: Matthew 11:15
text: Let him who has ears hear.

title: Matthew 11:16
text: But to what shall I compare the present generation? It is like little children sitting in the market-places and calling out to their playmates--

title: Matthew 11:17
text: 'We have played the flute for you, but you have not danced; We have wailed, but you have not mourned.'

title: Matthew 11:18
text: For, when John came, neither eating nor drinking, men said 'He has a demon in him';

title: Matthew 11:19
text: And now that the Son of Man has come, eating and drinking, they are saying 'Here is a glutton and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax-gatherers and outcasts!' And yet Wisdom is vindicated by her actions."

title: Matthew 11:20
text: Then Jesus began to reproach the towns in which most of his miracles had been done, because they had not repented:

title: Matthew 11:21
text: "Alas for you, Chorazin! Alas for you, Bethsaida! For, if the miracles which were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

title: Matthew 11:22
text: Yet, I tell you, the doom of Tyre and Sidon will be more bearable in the 'Day of Judgement' than yours.

title: Matthew 11:23
text: And you, Capernaum! Will you 'exalt yourself to Heaven'? 'You shall go down to the Place of Death.' For, if the miracles which have been done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have been standing to this day.

title: Matthew 11:24
text: Yet, I tell you, the doom of Sodom will be more bearable in the 'Day of Judgement' than yours."

title: Matthew 11:25
text: At that same time Jesus uttered the words: "I thank thee, Father, Lord of Heaven and earth, that, though thou has hidden these things from the wise and learned, thou hast revealed them to the child-like!

title: Matthew 11:26
text: Yes, Father, I thank thee that this has seemed good to thee.

title: Matthew 11:27
text: Everything has been committed to me by my Father; nor does any one fully know the Son, except the Father, or fully know the Father, except the Son and those to whom the Son may choose to reveal him.

title: Matthew 11:28
text: Come to me, all you who toil and are burdened, and I will give you rest!

title: Matthew 11:29
text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly-minded, and 'you shall find rest for your souls';

title: Matthew 11:30
text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."

title: Matthew 12:1
text: About the same time Jesus walked through the corn-fields one Sabbath. His disciples were hungry, and began to pick some ears of wheat and eat them.

title: Matthew 12:2
text: But, when the Pharisees saw this, they said: "Look! your disciples are doing what it is not allowable to do on a Sabbath!"

title: Matthew 12:3
text: "Have not you read," replied Jesus, "what David did, when he and his companions were hungry--

title: Matthew 12:4
text: How he went into the House of God, and how they ate the consecrated bread, through it was not allowable for him or his companions to eat it, but only for the priests?

title: Matthew 12:5
text: And have not you read in the law that, on the Sabbath, the priest in the Temple break the Sabbath and yet are not guilty?

title: Matthew 12:6
text: Here, however, I tell you, there is something greater than the Temple!

title: Matthew 12:7
text: And had you learned the meaning of the words--'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned those who are not guilty.

title: Matthew 12:8
text: For the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath."

title: Matthew 12:9
text: Passing on, Jesus went into their Synagogue,

title: Matthew 12:10
text: And there he saw a man with a withered hand. Some people asked Jesus whether it was allowable to work a cure on the Sabbath- -so that they might have a charge to bring against him.

title: Matthew 12:11
text: But Jesus said to them: "Which of you, if he had only one sheep, and that sheep fell into a pit on the Sabbath, would not lay hold of it and pull it out?

title: Matthew 12:12
text: And how much more precious a man is than a sheep! Therefore it is allowable to do good on the Sabbath."

title: Matthew 12:13
text: Then he said to the man. "Stretch out your hand." The man stretched it out; and it had become as sound as the other.

title: Matthew 12:14
text: On coming out, the Pharisees plotted against Jesus, to put him to death.

title: Matthew 12:15
text: Jesus, however, became aware of it, and went away from that place. A number of people followed him, and he cured them all;

title: Matthew 12:16
text: but he warned them not to make him known,

title: Matthew 12:17
text: in fulfillment of these words in the Prophet Isaiah--

title: Matthew 12:18
text: 'Behold! the Servant of my Choice, My Beloved, in whom my heart delights! I will breathe my spirit upon him, And he shall announce a time of judgement to the Gentiles.

title: Matthew 12:19
text: He shall not contend, nor cry aloud, Neither shall any one hear his voice in the streets;

title: Matthew 12:20
text: A bruised reed he will not break, And a smoldering wick he will not quench, Till he has brought the judgement to a victorious issue,

title: Matthew 12:21
text: And on his name shall the Gentiles rest their hopes."

title: Matthew 12:22
text: Then some people brought to Jesus a possessed man, who was blind and dumb; and he cured him, so that the man who had been dumb both talked and saw.

title: Matthew 12:23
text: At this all the people were astounded. "Is it possible that this is the son of David?" they exclaimed.

title: Matthew 12:24
text: But the Pharisees heard of it and said: "He drives out demons only by the help of Baal-zebub the chief of the demons."

title: Matthew 12:25
text: Jesus, however, was aware of what was passing in their minds, and said to them: "Any kingdom divided against itself becomes a desolation, and any town or household divided against itself will not last.

title: Matthew 12:26
text: So, if Satan drives Satan out, he must be divided against himself; and how, then, can his kingdom last?

title: Matthew 12:27
text: And, if it is by Baal-zebub's help that I drive out demons, by whose help is it that your own sons drive them out? Therefore they shall themselves be your judges.

title: Matthew 12:28
text: But, if it is by the help of the Spirit of God that I drive out demons, then the Kingdom of God must already be upon you.

title: Matthew 12:29
text: How, again, can any one get into a strong man's house and carry off his goods, without first securing him? And not till then will he plunder his house.

title: Matthew 12:30
text: He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not help me to gather is scattering.

title: Matthew 12:31
text: Therefore, I tell you, men will be forgiven every sin and slander; but slander against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

title: Matthew 12:32
text: Whoever speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in the present age, or in the age to come.

title: Matthew 12:33
text: You must assume either that both tree and fruit are good, or that both tree and fruit are worthless; since it is by it's fruits that a tree is known.

title: Matthew 12:34
text: You brood of vipers! how can you, evil as you are, say anything good? For what fills the heart will rise to the lips.

title: Matthew 12:35
text: A good man, from his good stores, produces good things; while an evil man, from his evil stores, produces evil things.

title: Matthew 12:36
text: I tell you that for every careless thing that men say, they must answer on the 'Day of Judgement.'

title: Matthew 12:37
text: For it is by your words that you will be acquitted, and by your words that you will be condemned."

title: Matthew 12:38
text: At this point, some Teachers of the Law and Pharisees interposed. "Teacher," they said, " we want to see some sign from you."

title: Matthew 12:39
text: "It is a wicked and unfaithful generation," answered Jesus, "that is asking for a sign, and no sign shall be given it except the sign of the Prophet Jonah.

title: Matthew 12:40
text: For, just as 'Jonah was inside the sea-monster three days and three nights,' so shall the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

title: Matthew 12:41
text: At the Judgement, the men of Nineveh will stand up with this generation, and will condemn it, because they repented at Jonah's proclamation; and here is more than a Jonah!

title: Matthew 12:42
text: At the Judgement the Queen of the South will rise up with the present generation, and will condemn it, because she came from the very ends of the earth to listen to the wisdom of Solomon; and here is more than a Solomon!

title: Matthew 12:43
text: No sooner does a foul spirit leave a man, than it passes through places where there is no water, in search of rest, and does not find it.

title: Matthew 12:44
text: Then it says 'I will go back to the home which I left'; but, on coming there, it finds it unoccupied, and swept, and put in order.

title: Matthew 12:45
text: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in, and make their home there; and the last state of that man proves to be worse than the first. So, too, will it be with this wicked generation."

title: Matthew 12:46
text: While he was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers were standing outside, asking to speak to him.

title: Matthew 12:47
text: Someone told him this, and Jesus replied:

title: Matthew 12:48
text: " Who is my mother? and who are my brothers?"

title: Matthew 12:49
text: Then, stretching out his hands towards his disciples, he said: "Here are my mother and my brothers!

title: Matthew 12:50
text: For any one who does the will of my Father who is in Heaven is my brother and sister and mother."

title: Matthew 13:1
text: That same day, when Jesus had left the house and was sitting by the Sea,

title: Matthew 13:2
text: such great crowds gathered round him, that he got into a boat, and sat in it, while all the people stood upon the beach.

title: Matthew 13:3
text: Then he told them many truths in parables. "The sower," he began, "went out to sow; and,

title: Matthew 13:4
text: As he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.

title: Matthew 13:5
text: Some fell on rocky places, where it had not much soil, and, having no depth of soil, sprang up at once.

title: Matthew 13:6
text: As soon as the sun had risen, it was scorched, and, having no root, withered away.

title: Matthew 13:7
text: Some, again, fell into the brambles; but the brambles shot up and choked it.

title: Matthew 13:8
text: Some, however, fell on good soil, and yielded a return, sometimes one hundred, sometimes sixty, sometimes thirty fold.

title: Matthew 13:9
text: Let him who has ears hear."

title: Matthew 13:10
text: Afterwards his disciples came to him, and said: "Why do you speak to them in parables?"

title: Matthew 13:11
text: "To you," answered Jesus, "the knowledge of the hidden truths of the Kingdom of Heaven has been imparted, but not to those.

title: Matthew 13:12
text: For, to all who have, more will be given, and they shall have abundance; but, from all who have nothing, even what they have will be taken away.

title: Matthew 13:13
text: That is why I speak to them in parables, because, though they have eyes, they do not see, and though they have ears, they do not hear or understand.

title: Matthew 13:14
text: And in them is being fulfilled that prophecy of Isaiah which says--'You will hear with your ears without ever understanding, And, though you have eyes, you will see without ever perceiving,

title: Matthew 13:15
text: For the mind of this nation has grown dense, And their ears are dull of hearing, Their eyes also have they closed; Lest some day they should perceive with their eyes, And with their ears they should hear, And in their mind they should understand, and should turn--And I should heal them.'

title: Matthew 13:16
text: But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear;

title: Matthew 13:17
text: For I tell you that many Prophets and good men have longed for the sight of the things which you are seeing, yet never saw them, and to hear the things which you are hearing, yet never heard them.

title: Matthew 13:18
text: Listen, then, yourselves to the parable of the Sower.

title: Matthew 13:19
text: When any one hears the Message of the Kingdom without understanding it, the Evil One comes and snatches away what has been sown in his mind. This is the man meant by the seed which was sown along the path.

title: Matthew 13:20
text: By the seed which was sown on rocky places is meant the man who hears the Message, and at once accepts it joyfully;

title: Matthew 13:21
text: But, as he has no root, he stands for only a short time; and, when trouble or persecution arises on account of the Message, he falls away at once.

title: Matthew 13:22
text: By the seed which was sown among the brambles is meant the man who hears the Message, but the cares of life and the glamour of wealth completely choke the Message, so that it gives no return.

title: Matthew 13:23
text: But by the seed which was sown on the good ground is meant the man who hears the Message and understands it, and really yields a return, sometimes one hundred, sometimes sixty, sometimes thirty fold."

title: Matthew 13:24
text: Another parable which Jesus told them was this--"The Kingdom of Heaven is compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field.

title: Matthew 13:25
text: But, while every one was asleep, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and then went away.

title: Matthew 13:26
text: So, when the blades of corn shot up, and came into ear, the tares made their appearance also.

title: Matthew 13:27
text: On this the owner's servants came to him, and said 'Was not it good seed that you sowed in your field? Where, then, do the tares in it come from?'

title: Matthew 13:28
text: 'An enemy has done this,' was his answer. 'Do you wish us, then,' they asked,' to go and gather them together?'

title: Matthew 13:29
text: 'No,' said he, 'for fear that, while you are gathering the tares, you should root up the wheat as well.

title: Matthew 13:30
text: Let both grow side by side till harvest; and then I shall say to the reapers, Gather the tares together first, and tie them in bundles for burning; but bring all the wheat into my barn.'"

title: Matthew 13:31
text: Another parable which he told them was this--"The Kingdom of Heaven is like a mustard-seed, which a man took and sowed in his field.

title: Matthew 13:32
text: This seed is smaller than all other seeds, but, when it has grown up, it is larger than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that 'the wild birds come and roost in its branches.'"

title: Matthew 13:33
text: This was another parable which Jesus related--"The Kingdom of Heaven is like some yeast which a woman took and covered up in three pecks of flour, until the whole had risen."

title: Matthew 13:34
text: Of all this Jesus spoke to the crowd in parables; indeed to them he used never to speak at all except in parables,

title: Matthew 13:35
text: in fulfillment of these words in the Prophet--'I will speak to them in parables; I will utter things kept secret since the foundation of the world.'

title: Matthew 13:36
text: Then Jesus left the crowd, and went into the house. Presently his disciples came to him, and said: "Explain to us the parable of the tares in the field."

title: Matthew 13:37
text: And he answered: "The sower of the good seed is the Son of Man.

title: Matthew 13:38
text: The field is the world. By the good seed is meant the People of the Kingdom. The tares are the wicked,

title: Matthew 13:39
text: And the enemy who sowed them is the Devil. The harvest-time is the close of the age, and the reapers are angels.

title: Matthew 13:40
text: And, just as the tares are gathered and burnt, so it will be at the close of the age.

title: Matthew 13:41
text: The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather from his kingdom all that hinders and those who live in sin,

title: Matthew 13:42
text: And 'will throw them into the fiery furnace,' where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

title: Matthew 13:43
text: Then shall the righteous shine, like the sun, in the Kingdom of their Father. Let him who has ears hear.

title: Matthew 13:44
text: The Kingdom of Heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid again, and then, in his delight, went and sold everything that he had, and bought that field.

title: Matthew 13:45
text: Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a merchant in search of choice pearls.

title: Matthew 13:46
text: Finding one of great value, he went and sold everything that he had, and bought it.

title: Matthew 13:47
text: Or again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a net which was cast into the sea, and caught fish of all kinds.

title: Matthew 13:48
text: When it was full, they hauled it up on the beach, and sat down and sorted the good fish into baskets, but threw the worthless ones away.

title: Matthew 13:49
text: So will it be at the close of the age. The angels will go out and separate the wicked from the righteous,

title: Matthew 13:50
text: And 'will throw them into the fiery furnace,' where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

title: Matthew 13:51
text: Have you understood all this?" Jesus asked. "Yes," they answered.

title: Matthew 13:52
text: Then he added: "So every Teacher of the Law, who has received instruction about the Kingdom of Heaven, is like a householder who produces from his stores things both new and old."

title: Matthew 13:53
text: When Jesus had finished these parables, he withdrew from that place.

title: Matthew 13:54
text: Going to his own part of the country, he taught the people in their Synagogue in such a manner that they were deeply impressed. "Where did he get this wisdom?" they said, "and the miracles?

title: Matthew 13:55
text: Is not he the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?

title: Matthew 13:56
text: And his sisters, too--are not they all living among us? Where, then did he get all this?"

title: Matthew 13:57
text: These things proved a hindrance to their believing in him; whereupon Jesus said: "A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country and in his own house."

title: Matthew 13:58
text: And he did not work many miracles there, because of their want of faith.

title: Matthew 14:1
text: At that time Prince Herod heard of the fame of Jesus,

title: Matthew 14:2
text: And said to his attendants: " This must be John the Baptist; he must be risen from the dead, and that is why these miraculous powers are active in him."

title: Matthew 14:3
text: For Herod had arrested John, put him in chains, and shut him up in prison, to please Herodias, the wife of Herod's brother Philip.

title: Matthew 14:4
text: For John had said to him 'You have no right to be living with her.'

title: Matthew 14:5
text: Yet, though Herod wanted to put him to death, he was afraid of the people, because they looked on John as a Prophet.

title: Matthew 14:6
text: But, when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced before his guests, and so pleased Herod,

title: Matthew 14:7
text: That he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.

title: Matthew 14:8
text: Prompted by her mother, the girl said 'Give me here, on a dish, the head of John the Baptist.'

title: Matthew 14:9
text: The king was distressed at this; yet, on account of his oath and of the guests at his table, he ordered it to be given her.

title: Matthew 14:10
text: He sent and beheaded John in the prison;

title: Matthew 14:11
text: And his head was brought on a dish and given to the girl, and she took it to her mother.

title: Matthew 14:12
text: Then John's disciples came, and took the body away, and buried it; and went and told Jesus.

title: Matthew 14:13
text: When Jesus heard of it, he retired privately in a boat to a lonely spot. The people, however, heard of his going, and followed him in crowds from the towns on foot.

title: Matthew 14:14
text: On getting out of the boat, Jesus saw a great crowd, and his heart was moved at the sight of them; and he cured all the sick among them.

title: Matthew 14:15
text: In the evening the disciples came up to him, and said: " This is a lonely spot, and the day is now far advanced; send the crowds away, that they may go to the villages, and buy themselves food."

title: Matthew 14:16
text: But Jesus said: " They need not go away, it is for you to give them something to eat."

title: Matthew 14:17
text: "We have nothing here," they said, "except five loaves and two fishes."

title: Matthew 14:18
text: "Bring them here to me," was his reply.

title: Matthew 14:19
text: Jesus ordered the people to take their seats on the grass; and, taking the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to Heaven, and said the blessing, and, after he had broken the loaves, gave them to his disciples; and they gave them to the crowds.

title: Matthew 14:20
text: Every one had sufficient to eat, and they picked up enough of the broken pieces that were left to fill twelve baskets.

title: Matthew 14:21
text: The men who ate were about five thousand in number, without counting women and children.

title: Matthew 14:22
text: Immediately afterwards Jesus made the disciples get into a boat and cross over in advance of him, while he dismissed the crowds.

title: Matthew 14:23
text: After dismissing the crowds, he went up the hill by himself to pray; and, when evening fell, he was there alone.

title: Matthew 14:24
text: The boat was by this time some miles from shore, laboring in the waves, for the wind was against her.

title: Matthew 14:25
text: Three hours after midnight, however, Jesus came towards the disciples, walking on the water.

title: Matthew 14:26
text: But, when they saw him walking on the water, they were terrified. "It is a ghost," they exclaimed, and cried out for fear.

title: Matthew 14:27
text: But Jesus at once spoke to them. "Courage!" he said, "It is I; do not be afraid!"

title: Matthew 14:28
text: "Master," Peter exclaimed, "if it is you, tell me to come to you on the water."

title: Matthew 14:29
text: And Jesus said: "Come." So Peter got down from the boat, and walked on the water, and went towards Jesus;

title: Matthew 14:30
text: But, when he felt the wind, he was frightened, and, beginning to sink, cried out: "Master! Save me!"

title: Matthew 14:31
text: Instantly Jesus stretched out his hand, and caught hold of him. "O man of little faith!" he said, "Why did you falter?"

title: Matthew 14:32
text: When they had got into the boat, the wind dropped.

title: Matthew 14:33
text: But the men in the boat threw themselves on their faces before him, and said: "You are indeed God's Son."

title: Matthew 14:34
text: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret.

title: Matthew 14:35
text: But the people of that place, recognizing Jesus, sent out to the whole country round, and brought to him all who were ill,

title: Matthew 14:36
text: Begging him merely to let them touch the tassel of his cloak; and all who touched were made perfectly well.

title: Matthew 15:1
text: Then some Pharisees and Teachers of the Law came to Jesus, and said:

title: Matthew 15:2
text: "How is it that your disciples break the traditions of our ancestors? For they do not wash their hands when they eat food."

title: Matthew 15:3
text: His reply was: "How is it that you on your side break God's commandments out of respect for your own traditions?

title: Matthew 15:4
text: For God said--'Honor thy father and mother,' and 'Let him who reviles his father or mother suffer death,'

title: Matthew 15:5
text: But you say 'Whenever any one says to his father or mother "Whatever of mine might have been of service to you is 'Given to God,'"

title: Matthew 15:6
text: He is in no way bound to honor his father.' In this way you have nullified the words of God on account of your traditions.

title: Matthew 15:7
text: Hypocrites! It was well said by Isaiah when he prophesied about you--

title: Matthew 15:8
text: 'This is a people that honor me with their lips, While their hearts are far removed from me;

title: Matthew 15:9
text: But vainly do they worship me, For they teach but the precepts of men.'"

title: Matthew 15:10
text: Then Jesus called the people to him, and said: "Listen, and mark my words.

title: Matthew 15:11
text: It is not what enters a man's mouth that 'defiles' him, but what comes out from his mouth--that does defile him!"

title: Matthew 15:12
text: On this his disciples came up to him, and said: "Do you know that the Pharisees were shocked on hearing what you said?"

title: Matthew 15:13
text: "Every plant," Jesus replied, "that my heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up.

title: Matthew 15:14
text: Let them be; they are but blind guides; and, if one blind man guides another, both of them will fall into a ditch."

title: Matthew 15:15
text: Upon this, Peter said to Jesus: "Explain this saying to us."

title: Matthew 15:16
text: "What, do even you understand nothing yet? Jesus exclaimed.

title: Matthew 15:17
text: "Do not you see that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the stomach, and is afterwards expelled?

title: Matthew 15:18
text: But the things that come out from the mouth proceed from the heart, and it is these that defile a man;

title: Matthew 15:19
text: For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts--murder, adultery, unchastity, theft, perjury, slander.

title: Matthew 15:20
text: These are the things that defile a man; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a man."

title: Matthew 15:21
text: On going away from that place, Jesus retired to the country round Tyre and Sidon.

title: Matthew 15:22
text: There, a Canaanite woman of that district came out and began calling to Jesus: "Take pity on me, Master, Son of David; my daughter is grievously possessed by a demon."

title: Matthew 15:23
text: But Jesus did not answer her a word; and his disciples came up and begged him to send her away. "She keeps calling out after us," they said.

title: Matthew 15:24
text: "I was not sent," replied Jesus, "to any one except the lost sheep of Israel."

title: Matthew 15:25
text: But the woman came, and, bowing to the ground before him, said: "Master, help me."

title: Matthew 15:26
text: "It is not fair," replied Jesus, "to take the children's food and throw it to dogs."

title: Matthew 15:27
text: "Yes, Master," she said, "for even dogs do feed on the scraps that fall from their owners' table."

title: Matthew 15:28
text: "Your faith is great," was his reply to the woman; "it shall be as you wish!" And her daughter was cured that very hour.

title: Matthew 15:29
text: On leaving that place, Jesus went to the shore of the Sea of Galilee; and then went up the hill, and sat down., you will do what not only what has been done to the fig tree, but, even if you should say to this hill 'Be lifted up and hurled into the sea!' it would be done.

title: Matthew 15:30
text: Great crowds of people came to him, bringing with them those who were lame, crippled, blind, or dumb, and many others. They put them down at his feet, and he cured them;

title: Matthew 15:31
text: And the crowds were astonished, when they saw the dumb talking, the cripples made sound, the lame walking about, and the blind with their sight restored; and they praised the God of Israel.

title: Matthew 15:32
text: Afterwards Jesus called his disciples to him, and said: "My heart is moved at the sight of all these people, for they have already been with me three days and they have nothing to eat; and I am unwilling to send them away hungry, for fear that they should break down on the way."

title: Matthew 15:33
text: "Where can we," his disciples asked, "in a lonely place find enough bread for such a crowd as this?"

title: Matthew 15:34
text: "How many loaves have you?" said Jesus. "Seven," they answered, "and a few small fish."

title: Matthew 15:35
text: Telling the crowd to sit down on the ground,

title: Matthew 15:36
text: Jesus took the seven loaves and the fish, and, after saying the thanksgiving, broke them, and gave them to the disciples; and the disciples gave them to the crowds.

title: Matthew 15:37
text: Every one had sufficient to eat, and they picked up seven baskets full of the broken pieces left.

title: Matthew 15:38
text: The men who ate were four thousand in number without counting women and children.

title: Matthew 15:39
text: Then, after dismissing the crowds, Jesus got into the boat, and went to the neighborhood of Magadan.

title: Matthew 16:1
text: Here the Pharisees and Sadducees came up, and, to test Jesus, requested him to show them some sign from the heavens.

title: Matthew 16:2
text: But Jesus answered: ["In the evening you say 'It will be fine weather, for the sky is as red as fire.'

title: Matthew 16:3
text: But in the morning you say 'To-day it will be stormy, for the sky is as red as fire and threatening.' You learn to read the sky; yet you are unable to read the signs of the times!]

title: Matthew 16:4
text: A wicked and unfaithful generation is asking for a sign, but no sign shall be given it except the sign of Jonah." So he left them and went away.

title: Matthew 16:5
text: Now the disciples had crossed to the opposite shore, and had forgotten to take any bread.

title: Matthew 16:6
text: Presently Jesus said to them: "Take care and be on your guard against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

title: Matthew 16:7
text: But the disciples began talking among themselves about their having brought no bread.

title: Matthew 16:8
text: On noticing this, Jesus said: "Why are you talking among yourselves about your being short of bread, O men of little faith?

title: Matthew 16:9
text: Do not you yet see, nor remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took away?

title: Matthew 16:10
text: Nor yet the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many basketfuls you took away?

title: Matthew 16:11
text: How is it that you do not see that I was not speaking about bread? Be on your guard against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

title: Matthew 16:12
text: Then they understood that he had told them to be on their guard, not against the leaven of bread, but against the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

title: Matthew 16:13
text: On coming into the neighborhood of Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked his disciples this question--"Who do people say that the Son of Man is?"

title: Matthew 16:14
text: "Some say John the Baptist," they answered, "Others, however, say that he is Elijah, while others again say Jeremiah, or one of the Prophets."

title: Matthew 16:15
text: "But you," he said, "who do you say that I am?"

title: Matthew 16:16
text: And to this Simon Peter answered: "You are the Christ, the Son of the Living God."

title: Matthew 16:17
text: "Blessed are you, Simon, Son of Jonah," Jesus replied. "For no human being has revealed this to you, but my Father who is in Heaven.

title: Matthew 16:18
text: Yes, and I say to you, Your name is 'Peter--a Rock, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the Powers of the Place of Death shall not prevail over it.

title: Matthew 16:19
text: I will give you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven. Whatever you forbid on earth will be held in Heaven to be forbidden, and whatever you allow on earth will be held in Heaven to be allowed."

title: Matthew 16:20
text: Then he charged his disciples not to tell any one that he was the Christ.

title: Matthew 16:21
text: At that time Jesus Christ began to explain to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, and undergo much suffering at the hands of the Councillors, and Chief Priests, and Teachers of the Law, and be put to death, and rise on the third day.

title: Matthew 16:22
text: But Peter took Jesus aside, and began to rebuke him. "Master," he said, "please God that shall never be your fate!"

title: Matthew 16:23
text: Jesus, however, turning to Peter, said: "Out of my way, Satan! You are a hindrance to me; for you look at things, not as God does, but as man does."

title: Matthew 16:24
